SUPERIOR COURT OF NEW JERSEY
CHANCERY DIVISION - SALEM COUNTY
DOCKET NO.
F-011818-22
SHERIFF NO.
25000118
PLAINTIFF -
Freedom Mortgage Corporation
DEFENDANT -
Bryant Baker, ET AL.
By virtue of a Writ of Execution in the above stated action to me directed, I shall expose for sale at public venue at the Salem County Courthouse, situated at No. 92 Market Street, in the City of Salem, New Jersey on
Monday,
April 20, 2026
at
2 o’clock
in the afternoon, ALL the following lot, tract or parcel of land and premises, situate, lying and being in the Township of Pennsville, in the County of Salem and State of New Jersey, bounded and described as follows:
Municipality: Pennsville
County of Salem
State of New Jersey
Street and Street No.: 9 Fordham Road Pennsville, NJ 08070
Tax Block and Lot No.: Block 3221, Lot 5
Dimensions of Lot (approximately): 80FT. X 100FT.
Nearest Cross Street: Fort Mott Road
A full legal description of the premises can be found in the offices of the County Clerk and the Sheriff of Salem County.
The approximate amount of the judgment to be satisfied by said sale is the sum of $396,400.52 together with the costs of this sale.
The approximate upset price is $433,996.20.
The upset price may be subject to further Orders of additional sums.
Subject to any unpaid taxes, municipal liens or other charges, and any such taxes, charges, liens, insurance premiums or other advances made by Plaintiff prior to this sale. All interested parties are to conduct and rely upon their own independent investigation to ascertain whether or not any outstanding interests remain of record and/or have priority over the lien being foreclosed and, if so, the current amount due thereon.
If the sale is set aside for any reason, the Purchaser at the sale shall be entitled only to return of the deposit paid. The Purchaser shall have no further recourse against the Mortgagor, the Mortgagee or the Mortgagee’s attorney.
The occupancy status of the property is: Unknown
The sale of this property is subject to a Consent Order entered into between Freedom Mortgage Corporation and NJR Clean Energy Ventures II Corporation (“NJR”) Docket#F-011818-22, filed on September 12, 2023. The terms of the Consent Order include, but are not limited to, the following:
The Solar Equipment is personal property owned by NJR and is not subject to the mortgage upon which the Bank is foreclosing. The Solar Equipment shall be excluded from the description of the Property sold at Sheriff’s Sale.
Following the (i) delivery of the deed to the purchaser at the Sheriff's Sale (if the purchaser at the Sheriff's Sale is not by the Bank or an affiliate), or (ii) the date that the Bank or a Bank affiliate executes an agreement to sell the Property to an unaffiliated third party (such purchaser at Sheriff’s Sale or unaffiliated contract purchaser is hereinafter referred to as the “Property Buyer”), NJR may negotiate with the Property Buyer regarding a new lease for the Solar Agreement (a “New Lease”).
The Bank and NJR shall provide such further assurances and cooperate as reasonably requested by NJR and the Property Buyer, or their respective successors and assigns, and shall execute such further documents, agreements, instruments, acknowledgments and certifications as may be reasonably requested to confirm the terms of this Order, including without limitation any documents, agreements, instruments, acknowledgments and certifications as may be required by an electrical utility provider or by the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities.
Terms of Sale: 20% of bid in cash, certified check or cashiers check from the successful bidder upon conclusion of sale. The Sheriff’s Office cash limit is $1,000.00 The balance is due within 30 days of the date of sale.
Surplus Money:
If after the sale and satisfaction of the mortgage debt, including costs and expenses, there remains any surplus money, the money will be deposited into the Superior Court Trust Fund and any person claiming the surplus, or any part thereof, may file a motion pursuant to the Court Rules 4:64-3 and 4:57-2 stating the nature and extent of that person’s claim and asking for an order directing payment of the surplus money. The Sheriff or other person conducting the sale will have information regarding the surplus, if any.
The Sheriff reserves the right to adjourn the sale without further notice through publication.
Brock & Scott, PLLC
, Attorneys for Plaintiff
Charles M. Miller, Sheriff
